terms.gloss: a property, a quality peculiar to a thing
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.56: singulārum rērum singulās proprietātēs esse

terms.gloss: a good quality, an excellence; in the plural, someone’s good qualities
evidence: Cic. Mur. 23: virtūtēs continentiae, gravitātis, jūstitiae, fideī (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: what is characteristic of someone or something
evidence: Tac. Agr. 42.4: proprium hūmānī ingeniī est ōdisse quem laeserīs
terms.comment: proprium est + genitive, it is characteristic of.
Cicero coined it for Greek ποιότης, a philosophers’ word even in Greek, as he says; frequent only in later prose (Lewis & Short). It does not by itself mean good quality.

phrases.english: that each single thing has its own particular qualities

phrases.latin: quālitātēs igitur appellāvī quās ποιότητας Graecī vocant, quod ipsum apud Graecōs nōn est vulgī verbum sed philosophōrum
phrases.english: so I have called “qualities” what the Greeks call poiotētes; and even among the Greeks that is not a word of ordinary people but of philosophers

sources: Lewis & Short: proprietas · Lewis & Short: virtus · Lewis & Short: proprius · Lewis & Short: qualitas
Cicero, Academica 1 and 2 (Lucullus), checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
